1) SAML NameID is capitalized in the assertion (J.Meyer@AsterialHealth.COM) which is not matching their Okta lowercasing rule -> login fails.
2) Coupa rejects the Tax ID as 'invalid format' even when it's entered as 123456789 or 12-3456789.

Thanks — this is blocking a $45k PO scheduled to be issued today.

Thanks for the context. Quick technical notes from the runtime/onboarding side:

- SAML NameID: Our SP metadata currently forwards the email attribute as provided by the IdP; we do not forcibly lowercase on-send. We can roll a quick change to normalize NameID to lowercase in the SP assertion transformer (low-risk config) but it will require a short deployment window (~30 mins) and coordination because it touches the assertion transform pipeline.

- Tax ID: The Coupa field validation is picky for some buyer tenants that enforce strict regexes per country. For US EINs we typically send the number without punctuation (123456789). If Asterial's tenant still rejects that, it looks like their tenant has an extra validation layer.

Workarounds (fastest to unblock PO):
1) Manual vendor creation by the buyer (Coupa admin) using the W-9 PDF. This will allow the PO to be raised to the vendor record immediately.
2) Send a non-SSO invite link (email-only acceptance) to bypass the IdP NameID problem while we deploy the NameID lowercasing change. Email-only invites are possible but will require creating a temporary token and updating the invite flow (I can generate this in ~15 mins).

If you want us to proceed with (2), we need Jason's confirmation to send the email-only invite to procurement@asterialhealth.com. If choosing (1) please confirm monica if legal has enough to create the record. Also capturing logs: please ask Asterial to forward the full SAML response (redact assertion signature) or provide an Okta syslog of the failed match.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
